Saturated δ blobs on det3: rails and a track + blob model

Generated by rerun/satstudy/make_satblob_report.py from satblob.py outputs. Golden row sat_det3 (6-27, 490 V), phys bundle, pre-pass final_phys table. Same 350 saturated views (≥ 3 saturated hits) + 150 unsaturated controls as satfit.py. Agreement with M3 = the C22 rule (|Δθ| ≤ 5° ladder-scaled, |p0 − M3| ≤ 3 mm).

The track + compact-blob model does not recover the saturated failures. On the saturated views, agreement with M3 goes 71.1 % (production) → 73.7 % (track + blob, both rails); most of that step is the multi-start alone (73.4 %, +8 / −0 views), the blob itself moves +15 / −6 views against production. With ΔBIC > 0 a blob is added to 88.7 % of unsaturated controls (model error, not blobs); no ΔBIC threshold separates the two groups usefully (scan below). A 5 % model-error term makes it worse (70.0 %). The rail fixes on their own, production fit: per-channel top rail +5 / −3, bottom rail censored +2 / −3, both +6 / −2 (72.3 %); controls unchanged. Pinned to the M3 line, the same model has a higher χ² than its free optimum in 93.5 % of the still-failing views (median ×3.6, against ×1.7 on views that DO agree, where it only measures how stiff a bright-pulse χ² is to M3's own error): the failure is the model, not the optimiser. The displays show why: the saturated deposit spans 5–10 strips and several hundred ns, a short δ TRACK rather than a point, so one compact deposit cannot absorb it.

gained / lost: views that switch from disagree to agree (and back) against production on the same view. Arms prod/rail/bot/railbot are the production fit (wft.reco.fit_plane, pivot start) with only the censor mask changed; mt_* and blob_* are the analysis-side optimiser (satblob_core.py): every start of the view, track-only (mt) or track + one compact deposit kept when ΔBIC = n ln(χ²_T/χ²_TB) − 5 ln n > 0.

The rail facts

  • Raw strip maxima above 3800 sit exactly at 4095 (13 086 strips): the rail is 4095 − pedestal − CM per channel and sample (3650–3900 after subtraction), rebuilt from the pedestals and the block CM of every event (match to the stored waveforms ≤ 2 ADC, float16).
  • In the 350 saturated windows: 8,346 samples are censored by both rules; 521 are ≥ 3550 but below their own rail (real measurements production throws away) and 1,176 sit ON the rail but below 3550 (a clipped plateau the common mode pulled down: production fits them as exact data).
  • Bottom rail (raw ADC 0): 5,792 samples in 282 of 350 saturated windows (80.6 %), fitted as data by production.

Is it the optimiser or the model? Track pinned to M3

The same fit with the track fixed to the M3 line (p0, angle from the reference; t0, the depth profile and the blob free). If the pinned χ² is LOWER than the free optimum the optimiser missed the right basin; if it is higher, the model itself prefers the wrong line.

Three random saturated views that still disagree after the track + blob fit (both rails, ΔBIC > 0): M3 dashed red, production fit white, track + blob fit orange dash-dot, the blob's position and depth circled. Outlined: samples ≥ 3550 (red) and on the bottom rail (blue).

Angle residuals

What this does not rule out

  • One compact deposit only (3 depth bins, point-like transverse). A δ that travels several mm sideways, or two blobs, is outside the model.
  • The bench χ²/dof is model-error dominated (~35 on clean tracks, ~500 on saturated ones), so the Gaussian BIC is not a calibrated test: the false-blob rate on controls is the honest measure, and the threshold should be set from it.
  • 350 + 150 views, one chamber (det3), one run condition; the fits do not include the column guard (WFT_COL_GUARD) of the pass, as satfit.py's prod arm.
  • Agreement is against M3, which is itself wrong for ~0.8 % of tracks (bent between the doublets).
  • Event-level detection (both views, n_dropped) is not re-derived here: these are per-view numbers.
